page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core using an Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU cache architecture provides 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3 cache. Advanced CPU instruction sets include AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 extensions, AES-NI, and VAES encryption support. System memory consists of 256.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, offering a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while local instance storage is not included and discrete hardware GPU accelerators are absent.

In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high performance in memory bandwidth tests, achieving top-quartile results across cached and uncached block reads. Application metrics show throughput of 70.49 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and static web serving throughput of 68.72 GB per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Clang software compilation benchmarks also rank in the upper quartile. Conversely, stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests produce average middle-tier results, reflecting the burstable CPU allocation profile. Small 135M model LLM prompt processing achieves average throughput of 2125.48 tokens per second, but 7B model prompt processing drops to 27.64 tokens per second due to the lack of GPU acceleration.

The burstable CPU allocation model provides qualitative cost advantages for workload patterns with variable compute demands rather than continuous sustained utilization. The combination of DDR5 memory performance, 64 vCPUs, and 12 Gbps network bandwidth makes this instance configuration appropriate for general web application serving, Redis in-memory caching, software compilation pipelines, and database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose burstable instance powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 256.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, and 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs. Instruction set capabilities include Intel AVX-512, AMX, and AES hardware acceleration. Benchmark data shows strong performance in memory bandwidth tests, software compilation, Redis SET operations at 70.49 million ops/sec, and static web serving at 68.72 GB/sec, alongside average stress-ng CPU scores attributable to its burstable allocation profile. The compute and memory ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for variable workloads. This instance fits application servers, in-memory caching, CI/CD compilation, and database workloads.
